requirements_summary:
Primary workload: low-latency chat + tool-calling for “natural language analytics” UI (interactive, user-facing). Secondary: batch summarization of dashboards/reports. They care about tail latency stability more than absolute best-case latency.

Performance targets (stated, subject to POC):
- First token latency: p95 <= 250–350ms (us-east) for typical prompts
- End-to-end latency: p95 <= 1.2s for common interactions (they cited ~200–600 output tokens; mix is spiky)
- Throughput: wants predictable tokens/sec under concurrency; will measure tokens/sec and queueing time separately
- Strong preference for dedicated capacity with stable scheduling behavior; they’ve been burned by “noisy neighbor” effects.

Observability expectations:
- Wants per-model + per-version dashboards: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, queueing vs execution breakdown, batch-size distributions
- Wants alerts that don’t flap; minimum sample sizes + dampening required
- Wants clear attribution: “kernel change vs scheduler batching vs infra fleet change”

Change management / regression detection questions:
- Asked directly: “Do you run an always-on performance canary in prod?” and “Can it gate rollouts automatically?”
- Wants to know how baselines are computed (rolling vs fixed) and how you prevent baseline drift from hiding regressions
- Wants confidence scoring / ‘how sure are you this is real’ on alerts + direct links to runbooks/traces

Security/compliance:
- SOC 2 required; SSO/SAML for console access
- Audit logs + retention controls
- KMS integration preferred for Dedicated (keys under their control); they asked about ‘no prompt retention’ / no customer data used for canary.

Deployment:
- Phase 1: Dedicated in us-east (VPC connectivity); Phase 2: possible EU region for EU customers + data residency.

Model notes:
- Open to curated open models; they want the ability to pin model versions and have fallback to compatible variants during incidents/capacity events.
notes:
Key contacts (from calls/notes):
- VP Eng (buyer): focused on risk + reliability, wants contractual SLOs and a regression story
- Platform Eng lead (champion): wants deep metrics (queueing vs execution), reproducible baselines, and alert hygiene

What they said (paraphrased / partial quotes):
- “We can’t have a kernel update turn into a 2-week fire drill again.”
- “p95 is what we live and die by. If p50 is great but p95 regresses, our product feels broken.”
- “Show me how you detect regressions before my users do.”

Dedicated interest:
- Strong lean toward Dedicated for predictable throughput + isolation. Hosted API is acceptable for early dev but they expect to migrate production to Dedicated.
- Asked if Redwood can reserve capacity with region-level failover and clear rollback procedures.

SLO expectations (needs to be formalized):
- Wants p95 first-token and p95 end-to-end lat SLOs; also wants tokens/sec as a ‘capacity health’ signal.
- Asked about how Redwood defines paging thresholds vs warnings, and who gets paged.

Regression detection tooling discussion:
- We described Redwood’s production perf canary approach (synthetic prompts, per-model baselines, anti-flap).
- They want to see: example alert payload, example Grafana dashboard, and how it integrates with release gates.
- Concern: baseline drift / seasonality. They asked: “If the baseline slowly degrades, do we just accept it?”
- Asked for region/SKU specificity: “Can eu-west A100 behave differently than us-east H100 and not spam alerts?”

POC proposal (draft):
- 2-week POC on Dedicated (us-east), 2–3 target models, fixed prompt-shape distribution agreed upfront, collect metrics for p95/p99 and tokens/sec, include canary-style synthetic runs to validate regression detection pipeline.

Open questions:
- Confirm exact target model list + max context/output limits for their interactive UI.
- Clarify whether they need strict EU data residency in first contract or as expansion clause.
- Determine whether they require customer-visible status/perf incident comms commitments.

Internal:
- SE: Noah Patel pulled in to answer deep perf canary + baseline strategy questions.
- Product: Marissa Cole coordinating SLO language + rollout gates expectations.

Risk:
- If we can’t give them confidence on regression detection + rollback gates, they may stick with self-hosted (they mentioned ‘we can own the knobs’ even if it’s a pain).
